Participants reported their frequency of use of three types of multivitamins and single supplements of vitamins A, C, and E, calcium, iron, and zinc over the 2 years before diagnosis.

cases.excerpt: The authors examined the relation of use of multivitamins as well as several single vitamin and mineral supplements to the risk of prostate cancer risk among 1,706 prostate cancer cases and 2,404 matched controls using data from the hospital-based case-control surveillance study conducted in the United States.

effect_size.excerpt: Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for risk of prostate cancer were estimated using conditional logistic regression model. For use of multivitamins that did not contain zinc, the multivariable odds ratios of prostate cancer were 0.6 for 1-4 years, 0.8 for 5-9 years, and 1.2 for 10 years or more, respectively (p for trend = 0.70).

confidence_interval.excerpt: As shown in Table 4 , the ORs for 10 or more years of use of multivitamins/minerals that did not contain zinc were 1.2 (95% CI: 0.8, 1.9) for all prostate cancer (p for trend = 0.71), 1.5 (95% CI: 0.9, 2.6) for early stage prostate cancer, and 1.0 (95% CI: 0.5, 1.9) for late stage prostate cancer.
confidence_interval.location: Results, paragraph beginning “Because we found an association of prostate cancer risk with zinc use”; Table 4, all prostate cancer, 10+ row

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test was not performed because fewer than 10 studies were available. With a small number of studies, the test generally has insufficient power to reliably detect funnel plot asymmetry.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 1.01 (95% CI: 0.97–1.04), indicating no statistically significant association between multivitamin and prostate cancer\aggressive. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by low heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
